title: 10k soldiers Vs. 100k Horde. Looking for feedback on my prototype.
author: ModernGameDev
selftext:
This past weekend I made a couple of prototypes testing my backlog of ideas and I believe this one may have the potential to be my first *commercial* game. It's not too big of a scope, I believe I can finish it in about 6 months as well. This isn't my first game though, i made flash games and mobile games in the past but never made one to sell on steam.

This first prototype is called Mercy for now. This is my take on an incremental game where you play as a divine Paladin commanding 10,000 soldiers against a 100,000-unit Horde. Watch the war unfold and time your abilities (Heal, Shield, Rally, and Smite) at critical moments, then permanently upgrade your army and return stronger.

How long can you keep an army alive against an enemy that massively outnumbers you? The goal is to keep your army alive long enough to finally defeat the horde.

This is currently an early prototype, and I'm looking for players to test the core loop and give feedback.

you can play it here: [https://the-modern-game-dev.itch.io/mercy-prototype-v1](https://the-modern-game-dev.itch.io/mercy-prototype-v1)

Later I'm thinking of using the Tiny Swords asset pack for this game.

And no I'm not going to render hundreds of thousands of game object on one screen, that'll be insane haha.
